result: An STDP protocol pairing postsynaptic action potentials with visually driven presynaptic inputs bidirectionally modifies neuronal spiking responses in vivo depending on spike timing. Positive timing (post-before-pre) converted subthreshold responses to suprathreshold in over 50% of neurons (8/15), increasing average spiking by 0.11±0.06 APs per stimulus (p=0.01). Negative timing (pre-before-post) decreased spiking from 0.84±0.23 to 0.18±0.10 APs per stimulus (p=0.04, n=15). These changes were not explained by membrane potential depolarization or input resistance changes, and control experiments without pairing showed no significant changes.

result: STDP induction restructured neuronal responses across the receptive field, with suprathreshold response centers shifting toward the pairing position after positive timing protocols. The shift was strongly correlated with the initial distance from pairing position (R=0.81, p=0.008, n=9). Subthreshold response centers also shifted toward pairing position for positive timing (R=0.53, p=0.04), though less robustly. Negative timing showed non-significant trends away from pairing position (p=0.70).

result: Computational modeling demonstrated that presynaptic temporal jitter is necessary to reproduce in vivo STDP effects. Models with precise timing produced narrow STDP windows matching in vitro studies, but introducing 40 ms jitter produced biphasic membrane potential changes matching experimental observations, with peaks at 30-50 ms before and after pairing spikes rather than at t=0. The model also reproduced partial transfer of plasticity to neighboring stimulus positions assuming overlapping presynaptic populations.

This demonstrates that small subthreshold changes can have dramatic effects on suprathreshold output, consistent with prior in vitro studies showing reliable spike generation from complex waveforms and sensitivity to small current injections.

result: STDP rules can modify output patterns of sensory neurons, with single-spike timing playing a crucial role in sensory coding and plasticity. This bridges the gap between population-level receptive field plasticity and single-neuron STDP, extending prior knowledge from subthreshold to suprathreshold domains.
